claims.text: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is a eutectic high-entropy alloy containing FCC and B2 phases.
Intermediate-temperature aging enhances L12 ordering in the FCC domains of AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Intermediate-temperature aging produces jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries.
Aging near 600°C produces maximum ordering and jagged phase-boundary development.
Chemical-ordering kinetics and phase-boundary evolution are pronounced between 550°C and 750°C.
L12 ordering locally increases elastic modulus and antiphase-boundary energy.
The increased ordering and stiffness restrict dislocation cross-slip and force planar slip.
Jagged B2/FCC phase-boundary tips produce local stress concentrations.
Stress concentrations at jagged phase-boundary tips initiate cracks and lead to plastic instability and embrittlement.
Aging near 750°C develops more ductile transition zones along phase boundaries.
Reduced ordering and ductile phase-boundary zones improve slip transfer and restore toughness.
The alloy exhibits a non-monotonic ductile–brittle–ductile transition with aging temperature.
Toughness is minimal after aging near 600°C.
Below approximately 550°C, ordering is minimal and baseline toughness is retained.
Between approximately 550°C and 750°C, a brittle window is caused by ordering and jagged phase boundaries.
Above approximately 750°C, reduced ordering and ductile phase-boundary zones cause ductility recovery.
Conventional-alloy embrittlement is controlled primarily by grain-boundary segregation and brittle precipitation rather than chemical ordering or phase-boundary morphology.

contradictions.description: The material initial state is the as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy, but the stated baseline is instead a class of conventional alloys. This leaves the reference state for claims of toughness loss or recovery internally ambiguous.
